title: Restore and validate static image assets for offline MCP downloads

requirements.summary: Add all missing static image assets into frontend/public so the app renders without broken images after MCP download.
acceptanceCriteria: All image files referenced by src attributes in the current frontend codebase exist on disk under frontend/public at the expected paths (e.g., /assets/... and /assets/generated/...).
Running the app locally shows no broken image icons on Home, Products, Category, and Subcategory pages.
A re-run of the MCP download command produces a folder that includes these image files.

requirements.summary: Audit and fix frontend image src references to use correct absolute public paths and avoid external/temporary URLs.
acceptanceCriteria: No in the app points to an external URL for core site visuals (hero, logo, category banners, placeholders).
All pages that render category images (ProductsPage, CategoryPage, SubcategoryPage) successfully load images using the product taxonomy image paths.
Home page hero image loads from the local public asset path.

requirements.summary: Provide a repo-local developer checklist/utility to enumerate required static asset paths used by the UI during development.
acceptanceCriteria: There is a clear, repo-local way for a developer to see which static asset files are required by the current UI (e.g., a documented checklist or a small utility script/runbook).
The checklist/utility includes at least the hero image, the logo, category banner images, and product placeholder images.

file_operations.description: Create a developer-facing checklist/runbook documenting all required static asset paths used by the UI, including: /assets/generated/home-hero-saddle-editorial.dim_1600x900.png, /assets/generated/Screenshot_2026-02-15_at_3.36.48_AM-removebg-preview.dim_800x800.png, all cat-*.dim_1200x800.png category banners, and all prod-placeholder-*.dim_1200x800.png placeholder images.

Add a lightweight Node script that prints (and optionally verifies existence of) the required public asset file paths referenced by the app so developers can quickly detect missing assets before exporting/downloading.
Centralize a typed list of required public asset paths (hero, logo, category banners, product placeholders) that can be imported by the dev script/documentation to keep the list in sync with the UI.
